guide_zh.overview: Open-source Python library for AI browser agents, plus Browser Use Cloud: stealth browsers and a hosted agent API.

The open-source browser agent. Run it locally with any LLM, or on [Browser Use Cloud](https://cloud.browser-use.com): stealth browsers from $0.02/hour, top score (90.5%) on [Stealth Bench V2](https://browser-use.com/benchmarks/browsers).

# Navigate the web like a human does. Find an available slot, pick a date and time, handle the CAPTCHA, and book a driving test. ![Browser Use V4 booking a driving test](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/135885e8-1141-4e10-b719-bf690ae7d260) [Explore more demos and prompts ↗](https://browser-use.com/showcase)
> **AI agents and crawlers:** read [browser-use.com/llms.txt](https://browser-use.com/llms.txt) for the product map (open source, Browser Harness, Cloud browsers, Agents API, pricing) and [docs.browser-use.com/llms.txt](https://docs.browser-use.com/llms.txt) for the documentation index. Browser Use is the open-source browser agent (Python and TypeScript), a $0.02 per browser-hour cloud browser with stealth, CAPTCHA solving and residential proxies, and a hosted agent API. # Which Browser Use do I need? - **[Path 1: Fully Hosted Cloud](#path-1-fully-hosted-cloud):** Scale up with a fully hosted agent and browser. - **[Path 2: CLI](#path-2-cli):** Automate your own browser tasks. - **[Path 3: Python Library](#path-3-python-library):** Run the open source Browser Use agent locally from your own code. # Quickstart ## Path 1: Fully Hosted Cloud Scale browser automation with our hosted agent, stealth browsers, and infrastructure for profiles, recordings, and data policies. [Get started with the API ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/agent/quickstart) New Google, GitHub, or Microsoft signups get **$1 cloud credit**.
## Path 2: CLI Paste this prompt into Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, or your favorite agent. ```text Install browser-use with `uv tool install browser-use`, run `browser-use skill install` to register the skill, and connect it to my browser. If setup or connection fails, follow https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md ```
## Path 3: Python Library > **browser-use 1.0.** The agent writes Python against raw CDP in a persistent REPL, on [Pydantic AI](https://ai.pydantic.dev). Coming from 0.x? Read [MIGRATING.md](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/MIGRATING.md). Python 3.11 or newer. With uv, or pip in a venv: ```bash uv init --python 3.12 my-agent && cd my-agent uv add 'browser-use>=1.0.0rc4' # release candidate: plain `uv add browser-use` still gives 0.x until 1.0.0 export BROWSER_USE_API_KEY=bu_... # get one at https://cloud.browser-use.com/new-api-key ``` ```bash python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate pip install 'browser-use>=1.0.0rc4' export BROWSER_USE_API_KEY=bu_... ``` ```python from browser_use import Agent result = Agent('Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo').run_sync() print(result.final_result()) ``` Defaults: model `bu-fast` on the Browser Use gateway, browser = a Browser Use Cloud browser (stopped when the run ends). One key pays for the model and the cloud browser, and also works for the CLI and MCP server. A `.env` file works too. **Local browser, your model:** ```python from browser_use import Agent, Browser, ChatOpenAI agent = Agent( 'Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo', llm=ChatOpenAI('gpt-6-luna'), # OPENAI_API_KEY; or ChatOpenAI(model, base_url=...) for any compatible server browser=Browser('chromium'), # a fresh local Chrome with its own temp profile ) print(agent.run_sync().final_result()) # in async code: result = await agent.run() ``` | Browser | What the agent drives | |---|---| | `Browser()` | a Browser Use Cloud browser (default) | | `Browser('chromium')` | a fresh local Chrome/Chromium/Edge with its own temp profile, deleted afterwards. Headless when there is no display (Docker, CI); `headless=`, `executable_path=`, `user_data_dir=` (a profile dir kept between runs) | | `Browser('chrome')` | the Chrome you have open, with your logins (turn on chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging once) | | `Browser('chrome', profile='Work')` | a new Chrome on a temporary copy of your Chrome profile `Work` (sync off); your Chrome can stay open, except on Windows | Other models: `ChatAnthropic`, `ChatGoogle` (both built in), or any Pydantic AI model string such as `llm='groq:llama-3.3-70b-versatile'` (after `pip install 'pydantic-ai-slim[groq]'`). - **Typed results:** `Agent(task, output_model_schema=MyModel)` then `result.structured_output`. - **Uploads:** put files in `Agent(task, workspace=...)` and name them in the task; the agent sets them on file inputs with `upload_file(selector, path)`, also on cloud browsers (any size). - **Downloads:** files the browser downloads land in `agent.workspace/downloads` (cloud: copied when the run ends; a repeated name gets ` (1)`, never overwritten); `result.downloads` lists the run's files. - **Secrets:** `Agent(task, sensitive_data={'password': '...'})`, or `{'https://*.example.com': {'password': '...'}}` to type it only on that domain. The model types it with `type_secret('password')`; the value is replaced with `` in cell output, checkpoints, tool results, the task and the result. Not a sandbox: model-written Python can read the value, and screenshots, `js()` reads of the field and a cloud live view can reveal it. See the trust model in MIGRATING.md. - **Domain restrictions:** `Browser(allowed_domains=['example.com', '*.example.org'])` (or `prohibited_domains=`, `block_ip_addresses=True`) with the 0.x patterns, in every browser mode. A guard for an aligned model, not a sandbox: see the FAQ. - **Follow-ups:** `agent.add_new_task('...')` then `await agent.run()`; use `Browser(keep_alive=True)` to keep the same page between runs. - **Custom tools:** plain functions with `@tools.action('description')`, then `Agent(task, tools=tools)`. - **Ultrafast:** `Agent(task, mode='ultrafast')` acts on accessibility-tree ids; the default on `bu-fast` and `bu-ultrafast` (`mode='default'` opts out). - **Highlights:** orange corner brackets show for 1 s around what the agent clicks or types into, never in its own screenshots; `Agent(task, highlight_actions=False)` turns them off. - **Web search:** the agent gets `search(query, num_results=None, category=None)` (Browser Use web search, billed per search to your Browser Use key; each charge the response reports is added to `result.cost_usd`) with `Agent(task, web_search=True)` (off by default; needs a Browser Use key, and can't be combined with `allowed_domains`).
# Browser Use Benchmark v2 This [very hard benchmark](https://github.com/browser-use/benchmark) targets the hardest browser tasks. On easier tasks, even smaller models can achieve very high success rates. Results shown are from a 60-task subset of BU Bench V2. ## Integrations, hosting, custom tools, MCP, and more on our [Docs ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com)
# FAQ
Should I use the fully hosted cloud, CLI, or Python library? - **[Fully Hosted Cloud](#path-1-fully-hosted-cloud):** Send tasks through the API and let Browser Use run the agent, browser, and infrastructure. - **[CLI](#path-2-cli):** Give an existing agent (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, Pi, Cursor, etc.) browser access. You can use it interactively or in scripts. - **[Python Library](#path-3-python-library):** Run the open source agent in your own application, with custom tools, structured output, and your choice of model. The CLI and Python library can each connect to a local or cloud browser. A cloud browser hosts the browser; the fully hosted API runs the agent as well.
What's the best model to use? The default, `bu-fast` on the Browser Use gateway, is `gpt-6-luna` at medium reasoning. `llm='bu-ultrafast'` runs the same model at low reasoning on the priority tier (fastest), `llm='bu-smart'` a larger one. `ChatOpenAI('gpt-6-luna')` with your own OpenAI key runs the same model directly. See the [benchmark](https://github.com/browser-use/benchmark).
Can I use this for free? The Python library is free and [MIT-licensed](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/LICENSE). Model inference and hosted browsers are separate: API providers, including `ChatBrowserUse`, and Browser Use Cloud charge for usage. You can also use `Browser('chromium')` with a local model, e.g. Ollama through `ChatOpenAI(model, base_url='http://localhost:11434/v1', api_key='ollama')`.
Terms of Service This open-source library is licensed under the MIT License. For Browser Use services & data policy, see our [Terms of Service](https://browser-use.com/legal/terms-of-service) and [Privacy Policy](https://browser-use.com/privacy/).
How do I handle authentication? - **Local browser:** `Browser('chrome')` drives the Chrome you have open, with your logins; `Browser('chrome', profile='Work')` uses a copy of that profile; `Browser('chromium', user_data_dir='~/bu-profile')` keeps its own logins between runs. - **Cloud browser:** `Browser(cloud_profile_id='work')` keeps logins in a cloud profile; see the [profile sync guide](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/interaction-skills/profile-sync.md). - **Passwords:** pass them as `sensitive_data`; the model types them with `type_secret(name)` and their values are redacted from cell output, checkpoints, tool results, the task and the result. Not a sandbox: model-written Python can read them, and screenshots, page JavaScript and a cloud live view can reveal a typed value.
How do I solve CAPTCHAs? [Browser Use Cloud](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/quickstart) provides stealth browsers and proxies designed to reduce bot detection and CAPTCHA challenges. With the Python library, `Browser()` is a cloud browser by default. Cloud browsers also solve CAPTCHAs automatically, and the agent waits for the solver with `solve_captcha()` instead of clicking the challenge. `Browser(captcha_solver=False)` turns the solver off. Results depend on the site and challenge; no browser configuration guarantees that every CAPTCHA can be avoided or solved.
Can I limit which sites the agent visits? `Browser(allowed_domains=['example.com', '*.example.org'])`, `Browser(prohibited_domains=['evil.com'])` or `Browser(block_ip_addresses=True)`, with the 0.x patterns, on any browser. The browser helpers refuse a disallowed URL, the browser itself blocks main-frame navigations to it (link clicks, redirects, popups, JavaScript; all modes except `Browser('chrome')` attached to your open Chrome, where a second debugging connection would prompt you again), every tab still on a disallowed page after a cell is reset to `about:blank` (in `Browser('chrome')` only the agent's tabs, never yours), and the system prompt lists the domains. A bare domain in `prohibited_domains` also covers its subdomains. It is a guard for an aligned model, not a sandbox: requests an allowed page makes to other hosts (`fetch`, images, iframes) are not filtered, nor is the agent's own Python networking beyond `http_get` and its redirects. Run untrusted tasks in a container or VM. [MIGRATING.md](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/MIGRATING.md#domain-restrictions) lists exactly what is blocked in each mode.
How do I go into production? Choose how much you want to manage: - **Keep your agent code:** Connect the CLI or Python library to [cloud browsers](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/quickstart) for managed browser infrastructure, stealth, and profiles. - **Have us run the agent too:** Use the [fully hosted Cloud API](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/agent/quickstart) to submit tasks and retrieve results. You can also host the Python library and browsers on your own infrastructure.

## Telemetry The library and the CLI send anonymized usage telemetry (counts, timings, model and helper names, exception classes, hostnames of visited pages; never the task, results, code, typed text, secrets or page content). Turn it off with `ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false`. [TELEMETRY.md](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/TELEMETRY.md) lists every field.
